report.markdown:
# Ocean Depth Report

## Deepest Ocean Point

The deepest known point in the world's oceans is Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, which has an estimated depth of approximately 10,935 meters. [1][2]

## Disputed or uncertain

One source reports that a study estimated the depth of the eastern basin of Challenger Deep to be approximately 10,927 meters. [2]

## Sources

1. [The Deepest Point In The Ocean](https://www.worldatlas.com/oceans/the-deepest-point-in-the-ocean.html) — worldatlas.com, published 2026-10-06, fetched 2026-10-31
2. [https://www.iflscience.com/why-we-still-dont-truly-know-the-exact-depth-of-the-oceans-deepest-point-84713](https://www.iflscience.com/why-we-still-dont-truly-know-the-exact-depth-of-the-oceans-deepest-point-84713) — iflscience.com, fetched 2026-10-31

evidence.quote: NOAA places the estimated depth of Challenger Deep at 35,876 ft (10,935 m).

[...] Give it a quick Google and you’ll probably get an AI overview telling you that Challenger Deep is “approximately 10,935 meters (35,876 feet) or about 6.8 miles below the ocean surface.” The figure is likely taken from a 2021 study by NOAA oceanographers (although it's not immediately clear since LLMs are not keen on crediting the information they "summarise").
The deepest section of the Mariana Trench, and therefore the deepest point in the ocean, is Challenger Deep , itself located southwest of the US territory of Guam .
